LLM auditresponse for install.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>UNSAFE</decision>
<details>
The script is designed to be downloaded and executed directly via a pipe from `curl` to `sh`, as shown in the usage comment: `curl -sSL https://token2.com/path/install.sh | sudo sh`. This is a well-known anti-pattern because it executes unverified code with root privileges without any integrity checking.

More critically, the script downloads and installs prebuilt `.deb` or `.rpm` packages from a URL specified by `BASE_URL` (defaulting to empty, but overrideable). If `BASE_URL` is set to a malicious server, the script will silently install an unsigned, unverified binary package with root privileges. The script performs no signature verification or checksum validation on the downloaded `.deb` or `.rpm` files. This creates a trivial supply-chain attack vector: an attacker who compromises the hosting domain or intercepts the connection can serve a malicious payload.

Additionally, the script builds from source if prebuilt installation fails, but this does not mitigate the risk — it only increases the attack surface. The source build section installs system dependencies via the package manager without user confirmation, compiles code in the current directory (which could be tampered with), and enables a systemd service. The combination of auto-downloading binaries, lack of verification, and blind execution under `sudo` makes this script unsafe.
</details>
<summary>
Downloads and installs unsigned binaries without verification
</summary>
</security_assessment>

Status: UNSAFE

Summary: Downloads and installs unsigned binaries without verification

Details:

The script is designed to be downloaded and executed directly via a pipe from `curl` to `sh`, as shown in the usage comment: `curl -sSL https://token2.com/path/install.sh | sudo sh`. This is a well-known anti-pattern because it executes unverified code with root privileges without any integrity checking.

More critically, the script downloads and installs prebuilt `.deb` or `.rpm` packages from a URL specified by `BASE_URL` (defaulting to empty, but overrideable). If `BASE_URL` is set to a malicious server, the script will silently install an unsigned, unverified binary package with root privileges. The script performs no signature verification or checksum validation on the downloaded `.deb` or `.rpm` files. This creates a trivial supply-chain attack vector: an attacker who compromises the hosting domain or intercepts the connection can serve a malicious payload.

Additionally, the script builds from source if prebuilt installation fails, but this does not mitigate the risk — it only increases the attack surface. The source build section installs system dependencies via the package manager without user confirmation, compiles code in the current directory (which could be tampered with), and enables a systemd service. The combination of auto-downloading binaries, lack of verification, and blind execution under `sudo` makes this script unsafe.
